title: A low-energy effective Hamiltonian for Landau quasiparticles: II Application to the contact Fermi gas
abstract: This article follows up on arxiv:2511.15938, in which we developed a new renormalization scheme to construct a quantized theory of Fermi liquids. Here, we apply this formalism to a low-temperature atomic Fermi gas where the short-range interactions are fully parametrized by the s-wave scattering length $a$. We benchmark our renormalized theory by recovering known perturbative results on the static properties of the Fermi gas, such as the Lee-Huang-Yang expansion of the equation of state, the Galitskii expansion of the momentum distribution, and the Gor'kov- Melik Barkhudarov preexponential correction to the critical temperature. We then turn to the transport dynamics and demonstrate the presence of a preexponential correction to the speed of zero sound when including corrections of second order in $a$. Finally, we develop an efficient numerical method to solve the transport equation exactly, and we apply to study the crossover from the collisionless to the hydrodynamic regime in the density and polarisation response functions.
summary: This paper applies a sophisticated low-energy effective Hamiltonian formalism to study the physics of an interacting Fermi gas. It systematically calculates static properties and predicts corrections to dynamic quantities like zero sound velocity by analyzing the crossover between collisionless and hydrodynamic regimes. The methodology is crucial for understanding strongly correlated quantum gases near unitarity.
main_problem: To develop and apply a low-energy effective Hamiltonian formalism for Landau quasiparticles to study the static and dynamic properties of a contact Fermi gas at low temperatures.
main_result: The theory successfully recovers known static results (e.g., LHY expansion) and predicts a preexponential correction to the zero sound velocity, while also providing a numerical method to map the crossover between collisionless and hydrodynamic regimes.
method: The authors use perturbative renormalization techniques, including Schrieffer-Wolff unitary transformations, applied to the contact interaction potential. They solve transport equations numerically to analyze dynamic response functions.
model_or_system: The system is a two-component gas of ultracold fermionic atoms interacting via a short-range (contact) potential. The analysis focuses on the low-temperature regime and utilizes an effective Hamiltonian approach derived from renormalization group techniques.
key_observables: Equation of state, momentum distribution, critical temperature ($T_c$), zero sound velocity ($c_0$), density and spin response functions ($	ext{Im}[ ar{\chi}_p]$).
important_parameters: Low temperatures, scattering length $a$, Fermi wave vector $k_F$, collision time $	au$. The analysis is perturbative in the limit $a 	o 0$.
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on a perturbative expansion (e.g., second order in $k_F a$), which limits controlled results to weak coupling regimes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams (BEC-BCS crossover), the angular dependence of calculated integrals ($I_\Lambda, J_\Lambda$), and numerical crossovers of response functions ($	ext{Im}[ ar{\chi}_p]$) between hydrodynamic and collisionless limits.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the renormalization scheme for constructing the effective Hamiltonian. It then benchmarks this theory against known static properties before moving to dynamic calculations, focusing on zero sound velocity corrections and solving the transport equation across different dynamical regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous theoretical tools (effective Hamiltonians, systematic expansions) to calculate finite-temperature quantum many-body dynamics in ultracold atomic gases, bridging weak-coupling theory with complex transport phenomena.
